overall: The AG found no evidence the Clarksburg Select Board deliberated outside a posted meeting to add two Special Town Meeting warrant articles, so no violation; other allegations were not reached or declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board deliberated outside a properly noticed meeting to add two PILOT and personnel-related articles to the Special Town Meeting warrant.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that a quorum of the Board discussed the two articles outside of a properly posted meeting, and we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant challenged the July 28 notice topic 'Special Town Meeting – Discuss and Finalize Warrant' as insufficiently detailed about the warrant articles.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we make no formal finding regarding the sufficiency of the notice for the July 28 meeting, and instead review the allegation that the Board deliberated outside of a properly noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Town Administrator violated the Open Meeting Law in connection with drafting the warrant articles.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the Town Administrator is not subject to the Open Meeting Law, and we therefore decline to review any allegation that the Town Administrator violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Town failed to follow a 2007 Town Meeting article on pay grade and step policies for employees.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
